theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which of these is a public area in a hotel?
options: A guest bedroom on the second floor
The main lobby and the corridors outside the rooms
The linen store behind the housekeeping office
The walk-in fridge in the hotel's main kitchen

questions.stem: Why is a busy lobby usually given its deep clean early in the morning or late at night?
options: Cleaning chemicals only work when the air is cool
The night supervisor is the only person who can sign it off
Guests like to watch staff cleaning while they check in
There are fewer guests about to disturb or put at risk

questions.stem: While cleaning the stairs you see a loose, broken tile on one step. What should you do?
options: Put a warning sign or cone by it and report it at once
Stick it down yourself with tape so that nobody will notice
Leave it, as tiles are the maintenance team's problem
Pull the tile out and throw it away with the waste

questions.stem: Before you start cleaning a lobby, what should you collect and check first?
options: The guest list for the day, so you can greet guests by name
Only a broom, because the other tools are kept in the lobby
The right equipment, chemicals and PPE, all in good order
The front desk cash float, so you can give guests change

questions.stem: Why should you wear closed, non-slip shoes when cleaning public areas?
options: They look smarter than sandals in front of guests
They stop cleaning chemicals from staining the floor
They help prevent slips and protect the feet from spills
They let you walk faster between the lobby and the store room

questions.stem: You are about to mop the lobby floor. When should you put out the wet floor signs?
options: Before you start mopping, where people will walk
After the floor is dry, to show it has been cleaned
Only if a guest asks whether the floor is wet or not
Only when the supervisor is walking through the lobby

questions.stem: When should the wet floor signs be taken away?
options: As soon as you finish mopping, before the floor dries
At the end of the shift, whatever the state of the floor
When the first guest has walked over the wet area
When the floor is completely dry and safe to walk on

questions.stem: What is the safe way to lift a heavy box of supplies for the public toilets?
options: Bend at the waist with straight legs and lift quickly
Bend your knees, keep your back straight and the load close
Twist your body as you lift so you can turn towards the shelf
Hold the box at arm's length so it does not touch your uniform

questions.stem: You find a used needle behind a sofa in the lobby. What should you do?
options: Do not touch it by hand; use tongs or a sharps kit and report it
Pick it up carefully with your fingers and put it in the bin
Leave it where it is and say nothing so you are not blamed
Wrap it in a tissue and put it in your apron pocket to hand in later

questions.stem: A vacuum cleaner's cable is cut and the wires show. What should you do?
options: Wrap tape around the cut and carry on vacuuming
Use it only on the dry floors until the end of your shift
Unplug it, stop using it, tag it faulty and report it
Ask a guest to hold the cable away from the cut part

questions.stem: Where do you find full information about a chemical's dangers, the PPE to wear and first aid?
options: On the till receipt from the shop that sold it
On the hotel's guest information card
In the guest comment book at reception
On the label and the safety data sheet (SDS)

questions.stem: Why must bleach never be mixed with other cleaning products such as toilet cleaner?
options: The mixture becomes too thick to pour
Together they can give off a gas that harms your lungs
The mixture loses its smell and guests complain
The mixture turns the floor tiles a pink colour

questions.stem: The label says to mix 20 ml of floor cleaner with each litre of water. How much cleaner do you add to a 5-litre bucket of water?
options: 20 ml
50 ml
100 ml
200 ml

questions.stem: Why should you not use more chemical than the label says?
options: It wastes money and can leave a sticky, slippery film
It makes the chemical work much faster and much better
It is the only way to remove a strong smell
Extra chemical makes the water cooler to use

questions.stem: How should cleaning chemicals be stored?
options: In empty drink bottles so they are easy to carry about
In their labelled containers, closed, in a locked store
On the lobby shelf where guests can reach them
Next to the food in the pantry, where it is cool and dry

questions.stem: Cleaning chemical splashes into a co-worker's eye. What should you do first?
options: Rub the eye gently with a clean dry cloth to remove the chemical
Put eye drops from the first aid box in and carry on
Wait to see if the eye gets red before doing anything
Rinse the eye with plenty of clean running water and get help

questions.stem: What does the "contact time" (or dwell time) on a disinfectant label mean?
options: How long the bottle can be kept on the shelf before it goes off
How long you must wait before opening a new bottle
How long the surface must stay wet for it to kill germs
How long the cleaner can work before taking a break

questions.stem: Many hotels use colour-coded cloths and mops. Why?
options: To stop germs spreading from toilets to other areas
To make the cleaning trolley look bright
So that each cleaner can choose a favourite colour
So that cloths can be washed less often

questions.stem: In the colour code many hotels follow, red cloths are kept for which area?
options: Kitchen worktops and other food areas
Lobby desks, tables and chairs
Glass doors, windows and mirrors
Toilets and urinals in the washrooms

questions.stem: Why do many cleaners use two buckets when mopping, one with cleaning solution and one for rinsing the mop?
options: So the mop can be left standing in one bucket overnight to soak
Dirt is rinsed from the mop, so the cleaning water stays clean
So two cleaners can mop the same floor at the very same time
So that much less floor cleaner is needed over a whole week

questions.stem: What is the safest way to dust a high light fitting in the lobby?
options: Use an extension duster from the floor, or a checked stepladder
Stand on a lobby chair or a table so you can reach it quickly
Climb onto the reception desk while a guest holds on to your legs
Throw a damp cloth up at it until the dust falls off

questions.stem: When should you empty the bag or bin of a vacuum cleaner?
options: Only once a month, on the day the machine is serviced
When dust is coming out of the top
Before it gets too full, as the maker's instructions say
Never; the bag is made to stay in for the machine's life

questions.stem: In which order should you clean a room or area?
options: Bottom to top, and wet before dry
Top to bottom, and dry before wet
Floor first, then the furniture
Wherever is dirtiest, in any order

questions.stem: When mopping a lobby, where should you start?
options: At the door you will leave by, working inwards
In the middle of the room, working out to the walls
Anywhere, as long as you go over the floor twice
At the far side, working back to the exit

questions.stem: The lobby is busy and must be mopped. What is the best way to keep a path open for guests?
options: Mop one half at a time, leaving a dry path to walk on
Mop the whole floor at once and ask guests to wait outside
Mop only where guests are not standing, and skip the rest
Mop very quickly so it dries before anyone walks on it

questions.stem: What is the main reason for damp dusting (using a slightly damp cloth) instead of a dry duster?
options: The furniture stays wet longer and looks shinier
It uses up all the old cloths that are too worn to use
The dust is picked up instead of spread into the air
It means the furniture never needs polishing again

questions.stem: How should you clean the glass in the lobby's front doors?
options: Spray it with bleach and leave it to dry in the sun
Wipe it with a dry paper towel only, using no cleaner at all
Scrub it with a scouring pad and an abrasive powder
Use glass cleaner and a clean cloth or squeegee, top down

questions.stem: Which surfaces in a lobby or lift should be wiped and disinfected most often?
options: The ceiling and tall cupboard tops
Door handles, lift buttons and stair rails
The backs of paintings hung on the walls
The underside of the reception desk

questions.stem: Sand and dry leaves have blown onto a villa's tiled terrace. What should you do first?
options: Mop it with lots of water and floor cleaner straight away
Spray it with the garden hose towards the guest rooms
Sweep up the loose sand and leaves before washing
Vacuum it up with the indoor carpet vacuum cleaner

questions.stem: Why should you change the mop water when it gets dirty?
options: Dirty water spreads dirt and germs back onto the floor
Dirty water uses up more floor cleaner
The bucket will rust if dirty water stays in it
Guests can see the dirty water if they pass by

questions.stem: What should you do before you start cleaning a public toilet?
options: Lock the door from the inside so that no one can enter
Knock, check it is empty and put out a cleaning sign
Open the windows wide and switch off all of the lights
Pour bleach into all of the toilets and urinals at once

questions.stem: Why do you put toilet cleaner under the rim and leave it for a short time before brushing?
options: To let the toilet dry out before the next guest uses it
So the smell spreads through the whole washroom
So that the brush does not need to be cleaned after use
To give it time to work on germs and stains

questions.stem: Which order is best when cleaning a public washroom?
options: Mirrors and basins, then toilets and urinals, floor last
Floor first, then toilets, then mirrors and basins last
Toilets first, then basins and mirrors with the same cloth
Basins only, as the toilets are cleaned by the night shift

questions.stem: Which supplies are checked and refilled when servicing a public washroom?
options: Pens, notepads and the guest comment cards
Bottles of drinking water and clean drinking glasses
Toilet tissue, hand soap and the paper towels
Newspapers, magazines and tourist leaflets

questions.stem: Why do many hotels hang a signed checklist on the back of the public washroom door?
options: To tell guests the price of the cleaning products used
So guests can write their room number for a free drink
To show guests the opening times of the hotel's restaurants
To show when it was last cleaned and checked, and by whom

questions.stem: A guest tells you a toilet in the lobby washroom is blocked and overflowing. What should you do first?
options: Tell the guest it is not your job and carry on dusting
Close it off with a sign and report it to maintenance
Keep flushing it until the water goes down by itself
Mop round it and leave it open for other guests to use

questions.stem: You are cleaning a corridor and a guest walks towards you. What should you do?
options: Stop, step aside, smile and greet the guest
Keep working and do not look up at the guest
Ask the guest to walk round by the stairs instead
Tell the guest to wait until the floor is dry

questions.stem: A guest asks you where the beach shuttle leaves from, but you are not sure. What should you do?
options: Guess the place, so that the guest is not kept waiting long
Tell the guest you only clean and cannot help
Say you will find out, and check with the front desk
Point to the car park and hope the guest finds it

questions.stem: How should you check the lobby when you have finished cleaning it?
options: Ask the first guest who walks in to give you a mark out of ten
Look round it as a guest would, and put right anything missed
There is no need to check if you followed the schedule
Wait for the supervisor to find faults the next morning

questions.stem: A guest complains that the pool deck chairs are dirty. What is the best response?
options: Explain that the chairs were cleaned yesterday by the day staff
Tell the guest to use a towel on the chair and say nothing more
Ask the guest to make the complaint in writing at reception
Say sorry, clean the chairs at once and tell your supervisor

questions.stem: You find a phone left on a sofa in the lobby. What should you do?
options: Keep it safe in your own locker until the end of the week
Leave it on the sofa in case the owner comes back
Hand it to your supervisor or security to be logged
Look through the phone to find the owner's name

questions.stem: A person you do not know is walking through a staff-only corridor. What should you do?
options: Politely ask if you can help, and tell security if unsure
Ignore them, because security is not part of a cleaner's job
Shout at them to leave the building at once
Give them your master key so they can find their way

questions.stem: A bag has been left alone in the lobby for a long time and no one claims it. What should you do?
options: Open it to see what is inside it and who might own it
Carry it to the lost property store yourself
Kick it under a chair so that guests do not trip
Do not touch it; tell security or your supervisor

questions.stem: How should you handle the waste from lobby and terrace bins?
options: Push it down with your hand so more fits in the bag
Tie the bag, lift it by the neck and hold it away from you
Carry the bag against your chest so it does not split
Tip it all into one big bag with the kitchen waste and glass

questions.stem: What should you do at the end of a shift with mops, cloths and buckets?
options: Leave them wet in the bucket so they are ready for tomorrow
Put them away dirty, as the next shift will wash them
Wash, rinse and dry them, then store them in the cupboard
Throw them away and order new ones for every shift

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters SDS stand for?
What is the name of the mat at an entrance that catches dirt and water from people's shoes?
Bleach must never be mixed with which chemical, found in some glass cleaners, because together they give off a poisonous gas?
What do the letters PPE stand for?
What container is used for used needles and other sharp items found while cleaning?
What is the name of the book or record where items found in public areas are written down?
In which pattern should you move a damp mop across an open floor?
What one word means mixing a chemical with water to the right strength?
What tool with a rubber blade is used to pull water off glass doors and windows?
What is the name of the kit kept for clearing up blood or vomit safely?
What word is used for cleaning a surface with a product that kills germs, such as door handles and rails?
Which hazard word on a chemical label means it can burn the skin and eyes?
What is the name of the plan that lists which public areas are cleaned, how often and by whom?
What colour is the usual wet floor sign used in hotels?
What should you wear on your hands when you use cleaning chemicals?

essays.stem: Describe, in order, how you would clean and restock a public washroom in a hotel lobby.
essays.modelAnswer: First I collect my trolley with the right colour-coded cloths, toilet brush, toilet cleaner, disinfectant, glass cleaner, mop and bucket, refills and wet floor signs, and I put on gloves. I knock, check that the washroom is empty and put a cleaning sign at the door. I open a window or switch on the fan. I empty the bins. I put toilet cleaner under the rims and leave it to work. I clean from the cleanest to the dirtiest: mirrors, then basins, taps and dispensers, then the toilet seats, bowls and urinals, using the toilet cloths only for the toilets. I wipe and disinfect touch points such as door handles, flush handles and taps. I refill toilet tissue, hand soap and paper towels. Last, I mop the floor from the far end back to the door, with the wet floor sign out. I check the room as a guest would, sign the checklist and take the sign away when the floor is dry.
markingPoints: Prepares equipment, PPE and signs, and checks the washroom is empty
Applies toilet cleaner and leaves it to work while cleaning elsewhere
Cleans from cleanest to dirtiest, keeping toilet cloths for toilets only
Disinfects touch points and restocks tissue, soap and paper towels
Mops last from the far end, checks the work and signs the checklist

essays.stem: Explain why public areas are cleaned at set times, and how you avoid disturbing guests while you clean.
essays.modelAnswer: Public areas such as the lobby, corridors, pool deck and washrooms are used by many people, so they get dirty quickly and must be cleaned to a schedule. Big jobs, like mopping the whole lobby or vacuuming corridors, are done when few guests are about, such as early morning, late evening, or when guests are out at the beach. This means less noise, fewer people slipping on wet floors and less waiting. During busy times I only do light work, like emptying bins, wiping touch points and picking up litter. I keep my trolley tidy and out of walkways, and I keep cables out of the way. I work quietly and do not shout to co-workers. When a guest comes near I stop, step aside, smile and greet them. I mop half an area at a time so there is a dry path, and I put out wet floor signs. Guests should feel the place is always clean, but hardly notice the cleaning.
markingPoints: Public areas are busy, so they are cleaned often to a schedule
Heavy or noisy work is done at quiet times when few guests are about
Light work only at busy times, with trolley and cables out of the way
Works quietly, stops and greets guests, gives way to them
Keeps a dry path and uses wet floor signs

essays.stem: Explain how to use a cleaning chemical safely, from choosing it to putting it away.
essays.modelAnswer: I choose the right chemical for the job and the surface, for example a neutral floor cleaner for tiles and a glass cleaner for doors. I read the label and the safety data sheet (SDS) to learn the dangers, the PPE to wear, how to dilute it and the first aid. I put on gloves, and eye protection if there is a risk of splashes. I measure the chemical with a jug or dispenser and add it to the right amount of water, never guessing, because too much is wasteful and can leave a slippery film. I never mix two products, especially bleach with ammonia or with toilet cleaner, because they can give off a poisonous gas. I keep the area aired and use the product only for its job. When I finish, I close the container, wipe it, and put it back in its labelled container in the locked chemical store, away from food. I report any spills or reactions straight away, and follow the maker's instructions and the property's rules.
markingPoints: Chooses the right product for the job and surface
Reads the label and SDS for dangers, PPE, dilution and first aid
Wears gloves and eye protection, and measures the dilution
Never mixes products, especially bleach with ammonia or acid cleaners
Stores it closed, labelled and locked away from food, and reports spills

essays.stem: Describe how you would clean a hotel lobby, including the furniture, the glass doors and the floor.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by walking round the lobby to see what needs doing, and I collect my equipment, chemicals and PPE. I pick up litter and empty the bins. I work from top to bottom and dry before wet. First I dust high places such as picture frames and light fittings with an extension duster. Then I damp dust the furniture, the reception counter and the plant pots, and I wipe and disinfect touch points like door handles and lift buttons. I clean the glass doors with glass cleaner and a clean cloth or squeegee, working from the top down, and I polish off any smears. I vacuum rugs and sweep or dust-mop the hard floor. Then I put out wet floor signs and damp mop the floor, one half at a time, working from the far side back to the exit, so guests always have a dry path. Last, I put the furniture straight, check the whole lobby as a guest would, and put my equipment away.
markingPoints: Checks the area first, picks up litter and empties the bins
Works top to bottom and dry before wet
Damp dusts furniture and disinfects touch points
Cleans glass top down with glass cleaner and cloth or squeegee
Sweeps then mops in halves with signs, then checks the finished lobby

essays.stem: Explain how you would clean the outdoor public areas of a villa (the pool deck, terrace, steps and entrance), and what Jamaica's weather means for this work.
essays.modelAnswer: Outdoor areas are cleaned early in the morning before guests come out and before the sun is hot. I pick up litter, cups and glass first, then sweep up leaves, sand and dust with a stiff broom, because water on loose sand makes mud. I wipe the sun loungers, tables and chairs with a damp cloth and a mild cleaner, because sea salt and sunscreen build up on them. I check cushions and dry them if they got wet in the rain. I wash the pool deck and steps as the property says, keeping water and cleaner out of the pool, and I check for slippery patches of algae. In Jamaica the sun dries chemicals fast and can fade cushions, so I work in sections and store cushions in shade. Salt air rusts metal, so I wipe metal furniture often. After rain I sweep away puddles and leaves. I watch for insects, wasp nests and broken tiles, and I report them.
markingPoints: Cleans early before guests and the hottest sun
Picks up litter and glass, then sweeps sand and leaves before washing
Wipes furniture for salt and sunscreen, and cares for cushions
Explains the effects of sun, salt air and rain on the work
Keeps chemicals out of the pool and reports hazards such as algae, nests or broken tiles

essays.stem: A guest drops a glass of rum punch on the tiled lobby floor and it breaks. Describe what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: First I make sure the guest is not hurt and ask other guests to keep away. I put a wet floor sign or cone by the spill at once, or ask a co-worker to stand by it while I fetch my equipment. I do not pick up glass with my bare hands. I put on gloves and use a dustpan and brush to sweep up the broken glass carefully, including small pieces that may have slid away, and I put the glass in a box or a bag marked for broken glass, not in a plain bin bag, so no one is cut. Then I soak up the liquid with a cloth or mop and damp mop the area with floor cleaner, because rum punch is sticky and attracts ants. I leave the sign out until the floor is dry. I check that no glass is left by looking along the floor. I tell my supervisor and offer the guest help or a fresh drink as the property's rules allow.
markingPoints: Checks the guest is safe and keeps people away
Puts out a sign or guards the spill straight away
Never handles glass by hand: gloves, dustpan and brush
Puts glass in a marked box or bag, then mops the sticky spill
Leaves the sign until dry, checks for pieces and reports it

essays.stem: Explain how you check, clean and store cleaning equipment before and after a shift, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Before my shift I check my equipment. I look at the vacuum cleaner's plug and cable for cuts or burns, and I make sure the bag or bin is not full. I check that mop heads, cloths and brushes are clean and that wet floor signs are on the trolley. I make sure chemical bottles are labelled and closed. Anything broken or unsafe I tag as faulty and report, and I do not use it. After the shift I empty the buckets, wash and rinse them and leave them upside down to dry. I rinse mop heads and send cloths to be washed, keeping the colour codes apart. I empty the vacuum, wipe it, and wind the cable loosely. I restock the trolley and put everything away in the cleaning store. This matters because dirty equipment spreads germs, faulty electrical equipment can give a shock, wet mops smell and grow mould, and a tidy trolley saves time the next day.
markingPoints: Checks electrical equipment, plug and cable before use
Tags and reports faulty items and does not use them
Washes, rinses and dries buckets, mops and cloths, keeping colour codes apart
Empties and wipes the vacuum, restocks and stores equipment
Explains why: germs, shocks, mould and readiness for the next shift

essays.stem: Explain how a cleaner in the public areas helps to keep guests and the property safe and secure.
essays.modelAnswer: A public area cleaner is all over the property, so they see a lot. I keep my keys or key card on me at all times and never lend them. I do not prop open staff doors or leave store rooms unlocked. If I see a person I do not know in a staff-only area, I politely ask if I can help, and I tell security if I am not sure. If I find an item a guest has left, such as a phone or sunglasses, I hand it to my supervisor or security straight away so it can be written in the lost property log. I do not touch a bag that has been left alone for a long time; I report it. I never tell anyone a guest's room number or details. I report broken locks, lights that are out, damaged fences and gates left open. Being alert and reporting quickly helps keep guests safe and protects the property.
markingPoints: Keeps keys safe and does not leave staff doors or stores open
Politely challenges strangers in staff areas and tells security
Hands in found items to be logged; does not touch unattended bags
Keeps guest details private
Reports broken locks, lights out and other security risks

essays.stem: Explain why touch points such as door handles, lift buttons and stair rails need extra attention, and how you clean them.
essays.modelAnswer: Touch points are surfaces that many hands touch every day, such as door handles and push plates, lift buttons, stair rails, light switches, the reception counter and washroom taps and flush handles. Germs from one person's hands stay on them and pass to the next person, so illness can spread through the hotel. That is why they are cleaned more often than other surfaces, sometimes several times a day as the schedule says. To clean them I wear gloves. I first wipe off dirt with a cloth and a detergent, because dirt stops a disinfectant from working. Then I apply the disinfectant at the dilution on the label, and leave it wet for the contact time on the label so it can kill germs. I use a fresh, clean cloth for each area and keep toilet cloths for toilets only. I spray onto the cloth, not onto electrical buttons. I record the time on the checklist.
markingPoints: Names touch points correctly
Explains how germs pass from hand to hand through them
Cleans them more often, as the schedule says
Cleans off dirt first, then disinfects at the right dilution and contact time
Uses clean or colour-coded cloths, sprays onto the cloth near electrics, and records it

essays.stem: Describe the kinds of hazards and faults you might find while cleaning public areas, and how you would report them.
essays.modelAnswer: While cleaning I may find hazards that could hurt a guest or a worker, or faults that need repair. Examples are a wet or oily patch on the floor, a loose or broken tile, a torn carpet edge, a trailing cable, a light that is out on the stairs, a dripping tap, a blocked or leaking toilet, a broken chair on the terrace, a wasp nest, or a broken pool gate. First I make the area safe if I can do it safely, for example by putting a sign or cone by it or closing off a toilet. I do not try repairs that are not my job. Then I report it straight away to my supervisor or the maintenance team, by phone or on the maintenance or hazard report form. I say exactly where it is, what the problem is, and when I found it. I check later that it has been fixed, and I tell my next shift about it.
markingPoints: Gives several suitable hazards and faults
Makes the area safe first (sign, cone, close off) without unsafe repairs
Reports at once to supervisor or maintenance
Uses the proper form or log with location, problem and time
Follows up and passes it on to the next shift

practical1.title: Clean and restock a public washroom to hotel standard
practical1.brief: As a group, clean and restock a public washroom at the Centre (or the mock villa's guest washroom) to the standard of a Jamaican hotel lobby washroom. The assessor acts as your supervisor. Work in these stages: (1) collect and check the trolley, colour-coded cloths, chemicals and PPE, read the labels and measure the dilutions; (2) knock, check the washroom is empty, put a cleaning sign at the door and air the room; (3) empty the bins and put toilet cleaner under the rims; (4) clean mirrors, basins, taps and dispensers; (5) clean toilets and urinals with the toilet cloths only, and disinfect touch points; (6) refill toilet tissue, soap and paper towels; (7) mop the floor from the far end to the door with a wet floor sign out; (8) check the room, sign the washroom checklist, then clean and store the equipment. Every member leads at least one stage, and every member cleans at least one basin and one toilet while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the washroom is finished and the equipment is stored.
materials: Colour-coded cloths (as the Centre uses) and a toilet brush
Toilet cleaner, disinfectant, multi-surface cleaner and glass cleaner, with their labels and SDS
Mop, two buckets and wet floor signs
Refills: toilet tissue, hand soap, paper towels and bin liners
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The trolley set up, with chemicals labelled and the measured solution
The cleaning sign at the washroom door
A toilet and urinal finished, with the toilet cloths kept apart
Dispensers refilled with tissue, soap and paper towels
The floor being mopped with the wet floor sign out
The signed checklist and the equipment cleaned and stored
checklist: Wore gloves and other PPE correctly and read the label before using each chemical
Measured the dilution with a jug, and did not mix products
Checked the washroom was empty and put out a sign before starting
Cleaned from cleanest to dirtiest, keeping toilet cloths for toilets only
Wiped and disinfected touch points such as handles, taps and flush handles
Refilled tissue, soap and paper towels and emptied the bins
Mopped from the far end towards the door with a wet floor sign out
Checked the finished washroom and signed the checklist correctly
Washed, dried and stored the equipment, and took a full part in the group
safety: Never mix chemicals, especially bleach with toilet cleaner or ammonia; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Wear gloves, and safety glasses when diluting or using toilet cleaner
Keep the room aired while using chemicals
Keep wet floor signs out until the floor is dry
Never pick up needles or broken glass by hand; tell the assessor
Lift boxes of refills with bent knees and a straight back

practical2.title: Clean a villa entrance, living area and corridor while guests are about
practical2.brief: As a group, clean the entrance, living area and corridor of the Centre's mock villa (or the Centre's foyer and corridor) as public areas, while the assessor and helpers play guests passing through. Work in these stages: (1) walk through the area, list the tasks and share them out; (2) collect and check equipment, chemicals and PPE; (3) pick up litter and empty the bins, keeping recycling apart; (4) dust from high to low with an extension duster and damp cloths; (5) clean the glass door or windows and disinfect the touch points; (6) vacuum the rugs, then sweep and mop the hard floor one half at a time with wet floor signs, keeping a dry path; (7) deal with a guest who asks a question and with an item the assessor has left behind, and write it in a lost property log; (8) write up on a hazard report form any hazards or faults you find (the assessor will have set up some); (9) check the area as a guest would, then clean and store the equipment. Every member leads at least one stage and takes part in the mopping and the dusting. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Extension duster, damp cloths and a bucket
Glass cleaner, a squeegee and lint-free cloths
Neutral floor cleaner, disinfectant and a measuring jug
Vacuum cleaner, broom, dustpan and brush
Mop, two buckets and wet floor signs
Bin liners and a recycling bag
A lost property log sheet and a hazard report form
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The group's task list and who does what
Dusting high places with the extension duster
The glass door or window finished, with no smears
The floor being mopped in halves, with signs out and a dry path
The lost property log filled in for the found item
The finished area seen from the entrance, and the equipment stored
checklist: Helped plan the tasks and took the jobs agreed
Checked equipment before use, including the vacuum's plug and cable
Worked top to bottom and dry before wet
Cleaned glass and touch points correctly with the right products
Mopped in sections with wet floor signs and kept a dry path for guests
Stopped, gave way and spoke politely to the guest, and found out what they needed
Handled the found item correctly and logged it
Spotted and reported hazards clearly on the form
Left the area clean and tidy and stored the equipment
safety: Do not stand on chairs or tables; use the extension duster or a checked stepladder with someone holding it
Keep cables out of walkways and switch off and unplug before emptying the vacuum
Keep wet floor signs out until the floor is dry
Do not touch planted hazards that could hurt you; report them to the assessor
Read labels, measure dilutions and never mix products
